title: Aurora Financial on-prem sizing, arch Q&A, Terraform notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for the Aurora Financial on-prem/private deployment evaluation. Goal is to capture initial sizing, architecture Q&A, Terraform module notes, and a conservative upgrade plan. Audience: solutions engineering, infra, and Aurora infra/security reviewers.

High-level ask from Aurora:
- Self-managed deployment inside their PCI-scoped VPC in us-east-2-equivalent colo.
- Baseline production throughput target: 120 concurrent inference sessions, median request size 256 tokens, 95th percentile latency target < 250ms for small-medium models (<=13B).
- Support for model version pinning, encrypted at-rest, and audit logs forwarded to tenant SIEM (Splunk).
- Rolling upgrades with no more than 5 minutes of degraded throughput.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Aurora will provide a private BGP/VPN connection and an internal DNS zone; we will not manage their border firewall.
- Storage for model artifacts will be on their object store (S3-compatible) accessible to nodes over 10GbE.
- GPUs available in their racks are NVIDIA H100 or A100 (T4 is allowed for non-critical workloads).
- Initial dataset/model weights ~600GB per served model (quantized variants can reduce to ~120GB).
- We are responsible for deployment orchestration (Terraform + Helm charts), health checks, and day-2 ops runbook.

Sizing recommendation (initial cluster, HA):
- Control plane / management: 3x m5.large-like VMs (or equivalent) for control-plane services (leader election, orchestration proxies); small and redundant.
- Serving nodes (GPU):
  - 6x H100 nodes (8x H100 would be ideal) configured as: 3 nodes in AZ-A, 3 in AZ-B for intra-site HA. Expect ~20-25 concurrent medium sessions per H100 with batching.
  - Fallback pool: 2x A100 nodes to absorb bursts; can be lower-cost.
- KV/cache nodes: 3x r5.4xlarge-like instances for Redis/kv-cache (replicated).
- Storage:
  - Model artifact NFS/CEPH backed mount: 5TB usable (to hold multiple models/versions); ensure throughput 2GB/s.
  - Logs: dedicated log volume (100GB) with daily rotation -> Splunk forwarder.
- Network: 25GbE per GPU node recommended. Internal network policy to reserve 40% capacity for KV/cache traffic and model fetches.

Why these numbers?
- 120 concurrent sessions / 6 H100 gives ~20 sessions per GPU, leaves headroom for batching inefficiencies, SLOs, and model warming.
- Redis cluster sized for KV cache hit rate target >= 85%.

Architecture Q&A (Aurora & SE notes):
Q: Do we need a multi-AZ deployment inside their single colo?
A: Aurora runs two logical racks in the colo; recommend distributing GPU nodes across both racks for rack-failure resiliency. Control plane remains three small VMs across both racks.

Q: Encryption key management? HSM?
A: Support both external KMS (Aurora IAM + KMS) and internal Redwood-managed KMS for POC. For PCI scope, Aurora prefers HSM-backed keys; integrate via PKCS#11/HSM connector. Call out: we need KMS admin contact and certs before the run.

Q: Which components store PHI/PCI data?
A: No PII/PHI should persist on Redwood nodes; request Aurora to validate that input data is filtered. Model logs may contain tokens; ensure token redaction in logging pipeline.

Terraform module notes (practical):
- Module layout: 
  - modules/networking (vpc, subnets, routing, nat, peering)
  - modules/k8s-cluster (if using k8s; otherwise modules/bare-metal-node-sets)
  - modules/serving (daemonset/statefulsets for runtime, autoscaler objects)
  - modules/kv (redis cluster provisioning)
  - modules/artifacts (object-store mount config, credentials)
- Providers: Lock to provider versions: hashicorp/aws ~> 4.50 (if using AWS-like APIs), hashicorp/kubernetes ~> 2.15. Always pin provider versions in module variables.
- State backend: remote state in Aurora's S3-compatible bucket + Dynamo-style locking (or HashiCorp Consul for on-prem locking). If Aurora cannot provide remote lock, use terraform's built-in state with lifecycle policies and manual locking guardrails.
- Secrets: do NOT store plaintext credentials in tfstate. Use Vault or Aurora KMS-encrypted secrets. Add a pre-apply hook to validate that credentials are referenced via data sources (vault_generic_secret or kms_decrypt).
- Example variables to surface: num_gpu_nodes, gpu_type, model_store_bucket, kms_key_arn, splunk_hec_endpoint, cluster_network_cidr, node_swap_policy.
- Automated runs: We recommend a gitops pipeline with Terraform Cloud or Atlantis for apply gating. If customer cannot host, runbooks for a controlled CI runner inside Aurora network.

Terraform gotchas we observed at other customers:
- Long drift windows when model artifacts get manually updated outside TF (use artifact immutability tags and CI checks).
- Provider auth tokens expiring mid-apply for long runs. Use short plans and apply via CI with refresh.
- NFS mounts introducing slow node boot times - pre-warm model downloads in init containers.

Upgrade plan (minor/patch vs major):
- Goals: No data loss, minimize throughput impact, maintain SLOs.
- Approach for minor/patch (runtime bugfixes, kernel/driver updates):
  1) Canary pool: create 1-2 canary nodes with new runtime, route 5% of traffic for 30 minutes.
  2) Monitor metrics (latency P99/P95, error rate, GPU memory usage). If stable, proceed with rolling replacement 1 node at a time.
  3) If regression detected, immediate rollback: divert traffic to previous pool and drain canary nodes.
- Approach for major (model architecture changes, large runtime changes):
  1) Blue/green: provision full green cluster alongside blue. Sync model artifacts via rsync or object-store copies.
  2) Warm caches by running synthetic warmers (script included in runbook).
  3) Switch traffic via load balancer or routing layer; keep blue for 72 hours for quick rollback.
- Upgrade timing: schedule during Aurora's maintenance window (usually Sun 02:00–06:00 local). Expect 1–4 hours for minor, 4–12+ for major depending on artifact distribution speed.

Rollbacks and runbook snippets (commands):
- Terraform safe apply: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply \"tfplan\"
- Draining a node (k8s): kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- Repointing traffic: curl -X POST https://infra-proxy.local/routing/switch -d '{"pool":"blue"}' (example for internal router)

Monitoring & SLOs:
- Instrumentation: Prometheus + Grafana locally, forward APM traces to Aurora's Jaeger/Zipkin if requested.
- Dashboards to include: per-node GPU utilization, per-request latency histogram, model-load times, cache hit-rate, error counts, Splunk HEC ingestion stats.
- Alerting: P99 latency > 500ms for 5m, error rate > 1% for 5m, node OOMs. Integrate with Aurora PagerDuty.

Compliance & audit logging:
- All admin actions recorded in audit log; forward to Splunk HEC.
- Signed attestations for software versions used in production. Maintain SBOM for runtime components.
- Endpoint access: TLS mutual auth for internal services; client certs rotated every 90 days.

Operational checklist before POC handover:
- [ ] Network handoff: confirm routes, firewall rules, and DNS entries (contact: Aurora-netops).
- [ ] KMS/HSM connectivity validated and test encrypt/decrypt.
- [ ] Storage performance validated: model fetch 600GB copy time within planned window.
- [ ] Canary tests: synthetic load run validates SLOs.
- [ ] Terraform remote state and locking in place.
- [ ] Splunk forwarder configured and test event received.
- [ ] Runbook and rollback steps validated with on-call.

Open questions / TODOs (needs Aurora input):
- Does Aurora require air-gapped installable images (OCI registry mirror)? If yes, provide mirror plan and image signing keys.
- Confirm exact GPU SKU and per-rack power/cooling constraints.
- Confirm whether Aurora wants Redwood to run node-level OS patching or hand over to their infra team.
- SLA expectations for Dedicated support window and on-call escalation.

Appendix: quick terraform variable example (for ops):
- variable \"gpu_type\" { type = string default = \"h100\" }
- variable \"num_gpu_nodes\" { type = number default = 6 }
- variable \"model_store_bucket\" { type = string }
- output \"serving_endpoint\" { value = module.serving.endpoint }

Notes to self / informal:
- Diego will prototype pre-warm container for large models (task: PRIVDEP-482).
- Rina to draft HSM integration checklist and cert procurement steps.
- Ethan to run rough-cost calc for Aurora (GPU amortization, power, network egress) and attach to this doc.
